<channel|>In a standard Transformer model, every parameter is activated for every token. As models grow to trillions of parameters, this becomes computationally unsustainable. Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architectures solve this by introducing conditional computation, where only a small subset of the model's parameters is used to process any given token.

The mechanism relies on a **router** (or gating network) located within the Feed-Forward Network (FFN) layers. When a token enters an MoE layer, the router performs a learned linear transformation on the token's hidden state to produce a probability distribution across all available "experts." Each expert is essentially a specialized FFN. Instead of passing the token to every expert, the router selects the top-$k$ experts (where $k$ is typically 1 or 2) with the highest scores. The token is then processed only by these selected experts, and their outputs are weighted and summed to form the final representation.
